# Semimartingale implementation-blocker ledger

This file gives the final disposition of `SM-B01`--`SM-B21` from section 18 of
*StochLean Semimartingale Core Design v0.1*.  It is the authoritative blocker
table; the older table in `docs/SEMIMARTINGALE_STATUS.md` is an append-only
historical snapshot and must not be used as the current disposition.

The three statuses have the following meanings.

- **RESOLVED**: the blocker named by the design has a production owner and a
  focused declaration-level audit (or, for a dependency rule, a repository
  dependency audit).
- **STILL-BLOCKED**: an exact source theorem or bridge is not claimed.  Any
  implemented core is named explicitly and is not promoted to the missing
  theorem.
- **DEFERRED**: the item is deliberately outside the implemented package
  boundary.  No theorem is inferred from adjacent infrastructure.

This documentation pass inspected the cited sources and audit harnesses; it did
not run Lean or Lake.

## Claim discipline

The matrix has 21 `RESOLVED` blocker rows.  For `SM-B20`, resolution means that
the exact numbered-source transcription and final-disposition task is complete;
it is not a claim that every source theorem has been proved.  The three
`STILL-BLOCKED` source bridges and the explicit `DEFERRED` scopes above remain
outside the public theorem inventory.

None of those boundaries invalidates an exported result.  The I.52 owners claim
RN existence/recovery and properties of a rational-liminf candidate, but not
their identification; the Jacod owner claims sigma-field and restricted-measure
lemmas, but not semimartingale preservation; the Meyer--Feller owner claims a
jump split, but not predictability of the complement.  Likewise, the classical
II.41, SII/Levy, and deterministic I.56 declarations retain hypotheses and
conclusions strictly inside their proved domains.  Future closure must add a
new theorem and focused audit; it must not reinterpret any existing core as the
missing result.
